scope: Read-only API and safety review of the current source-size refactor; no production changes in this review.

log_precision.conclusion: The removed LogTransform path is not required to support precision 2^24 on Clang/x86 or Mac. The existing generic block-division fallback retains the same precision.
log_precision.affected_region: 256 <= degree D <= 2^24, denominator size >=64; all other removed-path predicates unchanged.
log_precision.size_selection: Let S be ceil_power_of_two(D), optionally halved when D < 3S/4. Then S <= 2^24, B=S/32 <=2^19, L=2B <=2^20. B is a nonzero power of two because D>=256.
log_precision.transforms: The initial g.inv(B) requires transforms of at most B. The initial multiplication has output size at most 2B-1, hence transform length at most 2B=L. All later denominator, quotient, inverse and error transforms use L. Thus every length is <=2^20 < the existing NTT limit 2^23. No transform of length D is requested.
log_precision.inverse_without_avx2: On ARM or x86 without AVX2, inv(B) may call generic div_series. Its block size is at most B/16, so recursion strictly decreases until a small direct/Newton case. No larger transform is introduced.
log_precision.allocation_and_index_bounds: The count C=ceil(D/B) is at most48. pitch=L+16, and (2C-1)*pitch <=95*(2^20+16)=99,616,240 <2^27 <INT_MAX. Every slot offset and allocation-word product fits the existing int arithmetic. Actual allocation may remain large, as expected for precision2^24.
log_precision.integration: inverses(D-1) requires D-1 <mod=998244353; this holds for D<=2^24. Weighted derivative uses at most D coefficients and existing bounded loops.
log_precision.mathematics: Generic log_derivative forms x*f'(x), divides by f modulo x^D, and for log multiplies coefficient i by 1/i. With f[0]=1 this equals the original logarithm for every coefficient below D.
log_precision.maximum_precision_fixture: log_precision.cpp executed with Clang19 on the final frozen source, assertions enabled: all16,777,216 coefficients passed the independent closed form; checksum15647648346265480621. Source hashes unchanged before/after execution. See log_precision.json and log_precision.py.

other_review.public_api: No public FPS method signatures or return shapes were changed by the reviewed diff. Removed NTT methods are internal kernels; inverse_newton8 remains because its generic replacement regressed small-size performance. Standalone LogTransform remains available.
other_review.portable_targets: Removal of NEON paths selects existing scalar NTT behavior on ARM. Other large native kernels remain guarded by Linux x86_64 GCC !Clang conditions; no ARM intrinsics are introduced.
other_review.composition_range_invariant: composition_difference now shares difference(), which expects inputs <2p. Its companion composition_forward_y change replaces lazy radix4 with nonlazy stage_pair/stage, giving output <2p. These two changes must remain together.
other_review.evaluation_tree_shared_storage: BaseTree shared descent offsets are values_+8*(lo-lo_). BaseDescent leaves lo_=0 and retains global-output indexing. BaseInterpolation assigns lo_=lo per run and retains local indexing. The shared memory/product capacities are unchanged; the storage pointer is saved by the base constructor and first dereferenced only after complete object construction.
other_review.taylor_table: The generated constexpr table still contains all513 entries at step1024. uint64 product value*((i-1)*1024+j) is below 998244353*524288 <2^49, so generation cannot overflow. It adds no runtime initialization.
other_review.compaction: The active compact_fps change only lowers repeat-count eligibility from3 to2; existing token-boundary, protected-macro, literal, line-mapping and gain checks remain. New bundle fixture exercises twice-occurring code.
other_review.limitations: This is an independent code review, not a replacement for final platform builds, numerical validation, sanitizers or performance measurements. Any later native-kernel changes require their own final review/validation.
other_review.taylor_table_exact_value_check: All513 generated entries independently reproduced in Python and compared equal to the previous HEAD literal table.

shared_convolution_review.conclusion: No new API or safety defect found in the frozen shared-backend implementation.
shared_convolution_review.constructor_validation: Convolution::log_length rejects zero sizes and each operand >2^23 before evaluating n+m-1. Short-circuit evaluation bounds both sizes before summation, so size_t overflow cannot reach bit_width or allocation. It then rejects output size >2^23. Thus 6<=log_length<=23 and64<=len<=2^23 before member allocations.
shared_convolution_review.arena_capacity: Transform::words(lg) reserves exactly footprint(2*table_words(lg)); Transform constructor consumes that single span. The remaining arena budget has one footprint(len)=len+16 for borrowed a, or two for owned a and b. All accessed tails [len,len+16) lie inside their span footprints.
shared_convolution_review.borrowed_output: run_borrowed_as constructs len+16+7 live Mint elements, offsets to a32-byte boundary by0..7 elements, and hence retains at least len+16 elements after the aligned pointer. copy_input_mint writes exactly a.size() inputs; remaining result elements are initialized zero. After multiplication size<=len, so optional memmove and final resize remain inside live storage.
shared_convolution_review.copy_input_padding: copy_input reads full SIMD chunks only when i+8<=input.size(), handles tails scalarly, pads the necessary lower-half/full-length interval, and writes exactly16 extra words at len. The shared Source span contains the true input length, so any remaining upper-half arena bytes are treated as logical zero and are not read as input. Arena vectors are64-byte aligned; borrowed a is32-byte aligned.
shared_convolution_review.montgomery_scale: Inputs are Mint words xR and yR. Transform::cyclic_product with c=1 gives the ordinary raw polynomial product xyR^2: its existing inverse_scale(true) cancels the leaf Montgomery reduction. Passing c=R^-1 therefore gives xyR, the expected Mint representation. The correction is fused into the final existing scaling pass; append_fps_words<true> and borrowed output must therefore copy words directly. Both paths do so.
shared_convolution_review.subtree_weight_and_scale: New Subtrees forwards b using ForwardBottom and applies ProductBottom to a, both at the same absolute recursion index k as before. Both share the exact blocked_ntt root table and slot layout used by the removed clone. Recursion is unnormalized; no Transform final inverse scaling is added. Thus the existing Taylor outer inverse/scaling logic stays compatible.
shared_convolution_review.origin_bounds: For Subtrees::visit(nv,k), origin=k*nv is a vector index. Its bottom nodes cover g starting at k*nv/4. Every accessed b vector index4g+t-origin therefore lies in[0,nv). Recursive calls preserve the same absolute global-vector interval. Only the final nonnegative index difference is added to the actual b allocation; no pointer before the allocation is formed. Other ProductBottom aggregate initializers use the default origin0 and preserve their previous offsets.
shared_convolution_review.origin_callsite_audit: All ProductBottom b accesses in finish, InverseProductSumBottom, ForwardProductBottom and SideProductBottom subtract origin before pointer addition. InverseProductBottom a inputs and SideProductBottom side inputs retain their original whole-plan indexing; nonzero origin is only introduced for the b operand by Subtrees.
shared_convolution_review.portable_effect: The new Convolution/Subtrees implementation and ProductBottom.origin field are under Linux x86_64 GCC !Clang guards. The Clang/ARM mathematical fallback is unchanged by this additional backend sharing.
shared_convolution_review.verification_handoff: Final scoped GCC/Clang numerical tests, guard pages, sanitizers, official inputs and performance measurements run independently under the parent validation/benchmark tasks.
shared_convolution_review.maximum_precision_handoff: The additional Clang log endpoint run passed after final freeze; full evidence in log_precision.json.
